_source.desc:
# Welcome to Surat Hack 2026 🚀

**100+ Builders. One City. Endless Possibilities.**

Surat Hack 2026 is an AI-focused hackathon bringing together talented developers, students, entrepreneurs, and technology enthusiasts to build innovative solutions to real-world problems.

Whether you're an experienced developer, an AI enthusiast, or a student looking to turn your ideas into reality, this is your opportunity to collaborate, experiment, and build something meaningful.

## The Challenge

**Build an AI-powered application or agent that solves a real problem.**

From intelligent personal assistants and business automation to productivity tools and entirely new AI-native products, the possibilities are open.

We encourage participants to think creatively, experiment with emerging technologies, and develop working prototypes that demonstrate real-world value.

## What to Expect

- **18–24 hours of building:** Turn an idea into a working prototype.
- **100+ aspiring participants:** Connect with developers, students, and innovators from Surat and beyond.
- **Hands-on innovation:** Work with modern AI tools, APIs, and development frameworks.
- **Collaboration:** Build alongside talented people, exchange ideas, and learn from one another.
- **Project demonstrations:** Present your solution to a panel of industry professionals and experienced builders.
- **Networking:** Meet like-minded developers, entrepreneurs, and members of the local technology ecosystem.

## Who Can Participate?

Students, software developers, AI enthusiasts, working professionals, and aspiring founders are welcome.

You don't need to have founded a startup or built an AI product before. Bring your skills, curiosity, and willingness to create.

## Our Mission

Surat has an incredible community of ambitious students, developers, and entrepreneurs.

Our goal is to bring that community together, encourage practical AI innovation, and create opportunities for talented builders to showcase what they're capable of.

**Come with an idea. Leave with something you've built.**

Join us at Surat Hack 2026!

_source.tagline: The hackathon where Blockchain and AI meet
_source.location: House of Communication, Friedenstraße, Munich, Germany
_source.desc:
## The Theme: Agentic Payments

AI agents are starting to act on their own: booking, negotiating, paying. The payment rails for that don't fully exist yet. This hackathon is about building the infrastructure and applications that let autonomous agents transact safely and instantly on-chain.

## Format

- 30-hour build sprint
- Teams of 1 to 5
- ~200 builders on site
- Opening ceremony and partner track briefing on Friday morning
- Partner workshops, mentor office hours throughout the build
- Overnight build, lunch and dinner on site
- Live demos and judging

## Prizes

€12,000 across three partner tracks:

- **Cardano Track:** €6,000
- **BSV Blockchain Track:** €4,000
- **API3 Track:** €2,000

Pick a track, build against the partner's challenge, and compete for its prize pool.

## Details

- **Dates:** 30 to 31 October 2026
- **Venue:** House of Communication, Munich
- **Cost:** Free to participate. Accepted hackers also get a free ticket to all three days of TBC26.
- **Deposit:** Once accepted, you'll be asked to place a €50 deposit on Luma to confirm your spot.

## Why Build With Us

TUM Blockchain Club has brought together 3,000+ builders, researchers and founders over the last four years, running Europe's largest student-led Web3 event. This year the hackathon sits inside TBC26: three days, two venues, one community, with the main conference and Bundesblock's Digital Assets Day running alongside.

# HAXFINITY — Hack the Infinite

**The 24-hour hackathon of XTHRON ’26**

**12–13 December 2026**  
**10:30 AM on 12 December to 10:30 AM on 13 December**  
Amal College of Advanced Studies (Autonomous), Nilambur, Kerala

**Prizes:** Exciting prizes; details to be announced  
**Team size:** 2–4 participants  
**Participation:** Free, including the listed meals

**Build real solutions. Solve meaningful problems. Create something that works.**

HAXFINITY is the 24-hour hackathon conducted as part of XTHRON ’26, the annual IT fest of the Department of Computer Science, Amal College of Advanced Studies (Autonomous), Nilambur.

Across the event, students from different colleges and backgrounds will come together to identify problems, develop software solutions, build prototypes, and demonstrate their work to a panel of judges.

**The 24-hour event includes the opening ceremony, a 21-hour building window, project demonstrations, judging, and closing.**

There is no compulsory theme. Participants are free to choose a problem and develop a software solution using any suitable technology.

Whether you are an experienced developer or participating in your first hackathon, HAXFINITY is a space to learn, collaborate, experiment, and build.

## Prizes

**Exciting prizes await!**

Prize details and award categories will be announced once confirmed.

## Tracks

### Open Innovation

**Build something that solves a problem—or explore an idea you want to bring to life.**

You may work in education, healthcare, finance, agriculture, entertainment, productivity, cybersecurity, accessibility, sustainability, or any other domain.

There is no fixed problem statement or prescribed technology. Choose a problem or idea, design your approach, and build a prototype.

### AI / ML

**Explore intelligent systems and AI-powered applications.**

Use machine learning, generative AI, natural language processing, computer vision, recommendation systems, data analysis, or other AI-related technologies.

Demonstrate how the technology works, explain your implementation, and show what your team built during the event.

### Social Good

**Build technology that improves people’s lives.**

Possible areas include rural development, accessibility, mental health, financial inclusion, education, healthcare, environmental protection, and community welfare.

Focus on understanding the intended users and demonstrating how your prototype could address their needs.

*Detailed judging criteria and any track-specific award requirements will be published before the event.**
| Date and time               | Activity                                                             |
| --------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 12 December, 10:30–11:00 AM | Opening ceremony, rules, safety briefing, and event introduction     |
| 12 December, 11:00 AM       | Official project-building window begins                              |
| During the day              | Ideation, development, meals, mentoring, and technical support       |
| During the evening          | Continued building, dinner, and non-eliminating progress checkpoints |
| Around midnight             | Snacks, debugging, collaboration, and overnight building             |
| 13 December, 8:00 AM        | Submission deadline and code freeze; project development ends        |
| 13 December, 8:00–10:00 AM  | Submission checks, project demonstrations, and judging               |
| 13 December, 10:00–10:30 AM | Winners announced, prizes distributed, and closing ceremony          |
| 13 December, 10:30 AM       | Event concludes                                                      |

Building window: 21 hours, from 11:00 AM on 12 December to 8:00 AM on 13 December.

Meals, rest breaks, mentoring, and activities take place during the building window; they do not pause or extend the submission deadline.

Check-in instructions and any final schedule updates will be shared with registered participants. Every competing team will receive the same official building window.

## Who Can Participate?

HAXFINITY welcomes students from all academic streams and colleges.

Students from computer science, information technology, engineering, science, commerce, management, design, and other disciplines are encouraged to participate.

You are welcome whether you are:

- A beginner attending your first hackathon.
- An experienced developer.
- A designer or creative problem-solver.
- A student interested in AI, cybersecurity, cloud, web, mobile, or social-impact technology.
- Someone with an idea and the willingness to build it.

Come prepared to learn, collaborate, experiment, and contribute to your team.

## Team Details

- Each team must have **2–4 participants**.
- Solo competition entries are not permitted.
- Participants from different colleges may form one team.
- Participants from different academic streams may form one team.
- Interdisciplinary teams are encouraged.
- Each participant may be part of only one competing team.
- Every team member should actively contribute to the project.

## Venue

**Amal College of Advanced Studies (Autonomous)**  
Santhigramam, Eranhimangad  
Nilambur, Malappuram, Kerala — 679329

Directions, check-in instructions, and information about travel and overnight arrangements will be shared with registered participants.

## What We Provide

**Participation and the following provisions are free:**

- Dedicated workspace for participating teams.
- Power and internet access.
- Lunch on the first day.
- Dinner on the first day.
- Breakfast on the second day.
- Midnight snacks.
- Technical assistance during the event.
- Mentoring and guidance, subject to mentor availability.
- Participation certificates.
- An opportunity to demonstrate projects to judges and fellow participants.

Cloud credits, software benefits, merchandise, and other partner resources will be announced only after official confirmation.

#Competition Rules

- Teams must contain  2–4 participants.
- Project-specific development must take place during the official building window: **11:00 AM on 12 December to 8:00 AM on 13 December 2026**.
- Teams may arrive with an idea, but previously developed projects must not be submitted as new work.
- Participants may use open-source libraries, frameworks, APIs, publicly available datasets, and general-purpose templates, subject to their licences and usage terms.
- Teams must clearly disclose pre-existing components and distinguish them from work completed during HAXFINITY.
- **Generative AI and AI-assisted development tools are allowed across all tracks.** Teams must disclose the tools used, explain how they were used, and describe their own contribution.
- Projects must be submitted through **Devfolio by 8:00 AM on 13 December 2026**.
- Teams should upload their submissions early rather than waiting until the final minutes.
- Late submissions may not be accepted. Any event-wide technical exception will be communicated by the organisers.
- Teams must stop project development at code freeze. Adding new features after the deadline is not permitted.
- A working prototype or meaningful demonstration is expected. Teams should honestly explain incomplete or non-working parts.
- Teams must be prepared to explain their technology, development process, third-party components, and individual contributions.
- Progress checkpoints are for feedback and support—not elimination.
- Projects must not violate copyright, privacy, security, or applicable law.
- All participants must follow the event Code of Conduct.
- The organisers may disqualify entries for plagiarism, unsafe or illegal content, rule violations, or misconduct.
- Detailed judging criteria, demonstration instructions, and final competition rules will be published before the event.

## Code of Conduct

HAXFINITY follows the [MLH Code of Conduct](https://mlh.io/code-of-conduct).

Everyone is expected to help maintain a respectful, inclusive, and welcoming environment. Participants can approach the organising team for assistance or to report a concern.

***

12–13 December 2026
Amal College of Advanced Studies (Autonomous), Nilambur, Kerala

hackathon_faqs.question: Is there any registration fee to participate in GeNarrative Clash?
hackathon_faqs.answer: **No, participation is completely free!** There are no entry fees or hidden costs to register, build, or compete in the hackathon.

hackathon_faqs.question: Who can participate? Is the hackathon open to working professionals?
hackathon_faqs.answer: **GeNarrative Clash** is exclusively for currently enrolled university and college students. Working professionals are not eligible to compete as participants, though they are **welcome to join us as mentors or judges.**

hackathon_faqs.question: Do I need to be a Computer Science student to participate?
hackathon_faqs.answer: **Not at all!** Since this hackathon merges Generative AI with the creative arts, we strongly encourage students from design, media, literature, and other non-technical backgrounds to form teams with developers. **Diverse perspectives build the best tools.**

hackathon_faqs.question: Can our team have members from different colleges or universities?
hackathon_faqs.answer: **Yes, Cross-college and inter-disciplinary teams are absolutely allowed.** As long as every member is a currently enrolled student, you can team up with anyone you want.

hackathon_faqs.question: What is the allowed team size?
hackathon_faqs.answer: Teams can consist of anywhere from **2 to 4 members**. We highly recommend having a mix of technical developers and creative designers on your squad.

hackathon_faqs.question: Is the hackathon held entirely online or in person?
hackathon_faqs.answer: **It is a hybrid event.** The first round is online, where you will build and submit your 50% project prototype in between November 10th to November 16th . **The top 150** shortlisted teams will then be invited to Techno India University, Kolkata, on November 21st for the offline 6-hour hack sprint and live final pitches.

hackathon_faqs.question: What exactly do we need to submit for the online evaluation round?
hackathon_faqs.answer: Your online submission must include a **GitHub repository link** demonstrating at least 50% code completion, a clean and **comprehensive README file** explaining your tool, and a **live video demonstration link** showing your working prototype in action.

hackathon_faqs.question: What should we bring if our team is shortlisted for the in-person finale?
hackathon_faqs.answer: Bring your laptops, chargers, any specialized hardware you need, and a valid **college student ID card**. We will provide the **workspace, power outlets, Wi-Fi, and an AI masterclass to kick off the day.**

# GeNarrative Clash 2026
*Where Generative AI Meets Human Creativity*

Are you ready to redefine how stories are told, music is composed, and digital art is created? **GeNarrative Clash** is Kolkata's premier Prompt Engineering & AI Building Challenge, organized by the GeeksforGeeks Student Chapter at Techno India University.

---

### 🚀 Hands-On AI & API Masterclass (Included!)
Don't worry if you are new to AI development! Before the live challenge kicks off, every participant gets access to an exclusive **1-Hour Hands-On Masterclass on AI Development & API Integration**. Learn how to harness cutting-edge LLMs, query GenAI APIs, and leverage rapid prototyping tools so you can build a solid, production-ready product with confidence.

---

### 🎁 Perks, Bounties & Swag
* **Cash Bounties & Prize Pool:** Generous rewards or prizes for top-performing teams and winners.
* **Exclusive Swags:** Official sponsor goodies for top 12 finalists.
* **Certificates for All:** Official certificates of participation and achievement for all attending hackers.

---

### 🎨 The Challenge: Empowering the Creative Artist (Open Track)
Generative AI shouldn't replace human creators, it should supercharge them! **GeNarrative Clash** features an Open Track focused on building real-world solutions that assist, elevate, and support creative artists in their work. 

You are free to solve any real-world problem in the artistic or creative domain.

**Inspiration & Potential Project Directions:**
* **Storytelling & Narrative Assistants:** GenAI co-writers that help authors outline complex multiverses, generate dynamic dialogue, or build interactive narratives.
* **AI Music & Sound Studios:** Production-ready suites that assist musicians with harmonies, stem generation, or intelligent sound design.
* **Autonomous Creator Agents:** GenAI agents and social media co-pilots that help digital creators manage, format, and schedule content tailored to their target audience.
* **Digital Art & Visual Co-Pilots:** Tools that aid animators, illustrators, and designers in concept generation and workflow automation.

---

### ⚙️ Hackathon Rules & Technical Freedom
* **No Tech Stack Restrictions:** You are completely free to use any programming language, framework, API, or LLM (OpenAI, Gemini, Anthropic, or open-source models).
* **The 50/50 Pre-Building Rule:** To ensure high-quality, production-ready submissions, teams are permitted to pre-build up to **50% of their project before event day** (wireframes, boilerplate code, trained prompts, or baseline UI). The remaining **50% of the project must be built live** during the 6-hour hacking sprint.

---

### 📍 Venue & Event Date
* **Date:** November 21, 2026  
* **Venue:** Techno India University, EM Block, Sector V, Salt Lake, Kolkata, West Bengal 700091

# Hack With GDG S4

### 36 Hours of Innovation, Building, and Impact

**Hack With GDG S4** is the fourth season of the flagship hackathon organized by **Google Developer Groups – KSR College of Engineering (GDG KSRCE)**. The event brings together developers, designers, innovators, and problem-solvers to transform ideas into impactful solutions through technology.

## Important Update

Due to unforeseen circumstances, **Hack With GDG S4 has been postponed**.

**The revised dates for the hackathon will be announced soon.**

Participants are requested to follow our official communication channels for updates regarding the new schedule, submission deadlines, and other event-related announcements.

## Event Structure

### Round 1 — Ideation & Selection

Participants will submit their **project idea in PPT/PDF format** for evaluation.

Teams will be evaluated based on their problem statement, proposed solution, innovation, feasibility, and potential impact. A working prototype is not mandatory at this stage, but prior technical work may be considered an advantage.

Selected teams will advance to the offline hackathon.

### Round 2 — The Hack

Selected teams will participate in a **36-hour offline hackathon**, where they will build and demonstrate their solutions on-site.

Participants will have access to:

* Industry mentorship
* Technical guidance
* Networking opportunities
* Side events and activities
* Meals and refreshments throughout the event

## Who Can Participate?

Hack With GDG S4 welcomes participants across different skill levels and backgrounds.

* **Developers** — Build and implement innovative solutions
* **Designers** — Create engaging and user-friendly experiences
* **Innovators** — Identify real-world problems and develop meaningful solutions

**Team Size:** 1–4 members

Both **beginners and experienced participants** are welcome to participate.

## Themes & Innovation

The hackathon follows an **Open Innovation** approach. Participants are encouraged to identify meaningful real-world problems and develop technology-driven solutions across diverse domains.

## Rewards & Recognition

🏆 **Cash prizes** for winning teams
📜 **Participation certificates** for attendees
🤝 **Mentorship and networking opportunities**
💡 **Hands-on experience building solutions in a 36-hour environment**

## Venue

**KSR College of Engineering**
Namakkal, Tamil Nadu, India

**Event Format:** Offline
**Duration:** 36 Hours
**Dates:** **To be announced**

## Contact

For queries and further information:

**Email:** [gdgksrce@gmail.com](mailto:gdgksrce@gmail.com)
**Instagram:** @gdg_ksrce

### Stay Tuned

The **revised event dates and updated schedule will be announced soon**. Participants are encouraged to stay connected with GDG KSRCE for the latest announcements.

hackathon_faqs.question: What exactly is Hack 6.0 ?
hackathon_faqs.answer: It’s not just a hackathon—it’s an epic fusion of creativity, caffeine, and code! Think of it as a 36-hour sprint where brilliant minds come together to solve real problems, build cool stuff, and maybe win some brag-worthy prizes.

hackathon_faqs.question: Who can participate?
hackathon_faqs.answer: Whether you're a coding ninja, a design wizard, or just someone with crazy ideas—everyone’s welcome! Students, beginners, pros… if you’ve got the passion, you’ve got a spot here.

hackathon_faqs.question: How do I register?
hackathon_faqs.answer: Just click that big, shiny “Register Now” button on our website, fill in your details, and boom—you’re in! Don’t wait too long though; spots fill up fast!

hackathon_faqs.question: What if I don’t have a team?
hackathon_faqs.answer: No worries! We’ve got a team formation session before the hackathon kicks off. So, you’ll find your crew and maybe your next best friends.

hackathon_faqs.question: Who do I contact if I have more questions?
hackathon_faqs.answer: Hit us up at (csec@nith.ac.in) . We promise we’re super friendly (and quick to respond)!

hackathon_faqs.question: What is the procedure for participation?
hackathon_faqs.answer: Just register, and you will receive a confirmation email from CSEC before the event starts!

hackathon_faqs.question: Is there any registration fee?
hackathon_faqs.answer: No, participation in Hack 6.0 is completely free! 🎉 Just register and get ready to innovate!

hackathon_faqs.question: What about the accommodation for outside students?
hackathon_faqs.answer: On-campus accommodation will be provided for outstation participants! 🛏️🍽️ Details regarding lodging and meals will be shared after shortlisting.
